name: Arkansas
overview: In Arkansas the state, not the county, sells tax-delinquent land: real property forfeited to the state for unpaid real property taxes is certified to the Commissioner of State Lands, a state agency, which runs the public auctions county by county. Each county's auction is held once a year, in that county or a neighboring one. Anyone may redeem a certified parcel by paying the delinquent taxes until 4 p.m. on the last business day before the sale date; after that, parcels cannot be redeemed and sales are final. The buyer pays the full price on auction day and receives a limited warranty deed conveying whatever interest the state holds; parcels that do not sell are offered again through the Commissioner's post-auction sales 30 days later.

overview_sources.quote: We conduct public auctions of lands that were forfeited to the state for non-payment of real property taxes.
They are held once a year in the county where the property is located or in a contiguous county.
until 4 p.m. the last business day prior to the sale date
Parcels cannot be redeemed on the sale date or thereafter.
The state executes a Limited Warranty Deed, which conveys whatever interest the state has in the property to the purchaser.
Thirty (30) days after a public auction, parcels offered, but not sold, are available for sale through the Commissioner of State Lands office.

counties.how_to_bid: Attend the live public auction run by the Commissioner of State Lands. The full purchase price is due the day of the auction; cash is not accepted (personal or business check, credit or debit card, cashier's check or money order). No deposit is stated. Sales are final and the state conveys title by a limited warranty deed. Unsold parcels can later be bid on online at auction.cosl.org (the Commissioner's own post-auction site).
